newsitem.title: USA: World Bank reorganizes its Latin America division.
newsitem.headline: World Bank reorganizes its Latin America division.

text.p: The World Bank said on Monday it was restructuring its Latin America and Caribbean division and opening more offices in the region.
The World Bank's vicepresident for the region, Shahid Javed Burki, said that as of July 1 his division's four country departments will be regrouped into seven different offices.
"Our hope is that by having a greater presence in the field ... we will be able to cut down on the time we take to deliver projects," Burki told a news conference.
The World Bank makes loans for about $5.0 billion annually to countries in Latin America and the Caribbean.

Besides the office it opened last year in Mexico City to support programs in Mexico, the World Bank plans to open a Brazil office in Brasilia and another office in Buenos Aires that will handle Argentina, Chile and Uruguay.
The other four offices, which will remain in Washington, will cover the Caribbean; Central America; Bolivia, Paraguay and Peru; and Colombia, Ecuador and Venezuela.

The division will also have four sectorial departments to follow regional issues. Chief economist Guillermo Perry will be in charge of the poverty reduction and economic management unit. Another department will deal with finance and private sector investment, while a third office will cover environmental and sustainable development issues, and a fourth will be in charge of infrastructure.
